title: Bank Administrator
description: An opportunity has arisen to join the Kingston and Richmond Autism Service in a bank role as an Administrator within the Neurodevelopmental Service. Based at Hollyfield House, you will have a key role in the effective running of a busy service, with responsibilities including referral management, clinical appointments and supporting clinicians within the service. You will also answer queries about the service and will be confident and willing to communicate with neurodivergent people by telephone and face to face, as required. You will need to be well organised in managing clinic appointments, booking and review systems, and coordinating and sending out reports. You will be well supported and highly valued by the Autism Service and will receive regular supervision. The successful applicant will also provide some administrative support to the Adult ADHD Service, as directed by the service leads. Please apply using the NHS Jobs online system. Your application should explain why you are applying for the post, how you believe you would contribute to working in this setting and demonstrate how you meet the requirements of the person specification. Please be aware that the closing date may be brought forward in the event of a high number of applications. Were looking for someone who Has strong administrative and organisational skills, with excellent attention to detail. Can manage competing priorities and work calmly and efficiently in a busy service. Communicates clearly, sensitively and confidently by telephone, email and face to face. Understands the importance of confidentiality, accurate record keeping and timely information sharing. Works well independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Ideally has previous administrative experience within a neurodevelopmental, mental health or healthcare service. The usual working hours are 9am- 5pm and will be Monday Friday and there is some flexibility on the days the hours are worked. You will be based at Hollyfield Road in Surbiton although you will also need to be able to travel to our other sites as needed. We encourage you to discuss your flexibility needs with us before applying or during the interview process. While we may not be able to meet every request exactly, we promise to fully consider your needs and accommodate them where possible. Please note that flexible working options may vary depending on the role. When completing your application please refer to full Job Description - this can be found under supporting documents.

title: Receptionist / Administrator
description: Receptionist / Administrator Location: Parkview Surgery, 60 West Drayton Road, Uxbridge, UB8 3LA Hours: 16.5 hours per week Reports to: Reception Manager Please complete the attached Job Application Form and email it to k.barton8@nhs.net alongside your application. Applications without a completed form will not be considered. Interviews: Tuesday 10 November. Were looking for an enthusiastic, hardworking and approachable person with a positive attitude and a passion for helping others to join our busy practice. This varied role combines patient-facing reception duties with administrative work, helping patients access care and keeping the practice running smoothly. You'll be a confident communicator who listens carefully, puts patients first and handles difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism. Organised and adaptable, you'll respond to changing priorities and take pride in completing tasks accurately and efficiently. A willingness to learn our systems, follow procedures and act on feedback is essential. You'll join a welcoming team that values collaboration, open communication and initiative, with opportunities to develop your skills and make a difference to patients every day. Eligible employees can join the NHS Pension Scheme , with employee and employer contributions made in accordance with scheme rules. This varied role combines welcoming patients, handling telephone enquiries, booking appointments and processing prescription requests with daily administrative duties, including updating patient records, processing clinical documents and actioning emails. You will help patients access appropriate care and support the smooth running of the practice, working flexibly across reception and administration while maintaining accuracy, confidentiality and a professional, helpful approach. Main responsibilities Patient reception and communication Welcome patients and respond to enquiries in person and by telephone with kindness, patience and professionalism. Listen carefully, explain practice processes clearly and direct patients to the appropriate person or service. Remain calm during difficult conversations, help resolve concerns and seek support when needed. Take accurate messages and pass information promptly to the relevant team member. Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external services. Appointments and prescriptions Book and manage appointments in line with practice procedures. Receive and pass on home visit requests appropriately. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice guidelines. Administration and patient records Register new patients and update changes to personal details accurately. Maintain patient records using EMIS Web. Process clinical documents through Docman and EMIS in line with training and written protocols. File correspondence and support recalls for medical reviews. Monitor and action incoming emails, referring queries appropriately. Complete general administrative tasks, including photocopying and emailing. Organise and prioritise allocated work, completing tasks accurately and within required timescales. Teamwork and practice support Work flexibly across reception and administration, adapting to changing priorities. Support colleagues and provide agreed cover for staff absence and annual leave. Follow opening, closing and building security procedures. Keep work areas tidy, safe and organised. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. Professional responsibilities Maintain patient, staff and practice confidentiality at all times. Follow practice policies, written protocols and information governance requirements. Uphold equality, dignity and respect in all interactions. Follow health and safety, infection prevention and safeguarding procedures, reporting concerns promptly. Complete required training and participate in appraisals. Take responsibility for learning practice processes, acting on feedback and maintaining agreed standards. Contribute suggestions and participate in service improvements, practice meetings or audits when required.

title: Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised and proactive Administrator to join our friendly team, providing vital support across inpatient and community services. This is a varied role where you will be the first point of contact for patients, visitors and colleagues, helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of clinical and administrative functions. If you have excellent communication skills, enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, and are confident using Microsoft Office and other IT systems, we would love to hear from you. In return, you'll join a supportive team and play an important role in delivering high-quality patient care and services. Previous Applicants need not apply. Responsible for the day to day administration across intermediate with other members of the team. Responsible for supporting colleagues ensuring work is completed within an agreed timeline. Able to populate reports and collate data on agreed templates This role will act as point of contact for patients and visitors, this will entail being calm, professional and empathetic whilst dealing with potentially sensitive and stressfully situations. This role sits within Ealing Community Partners and will act as point of contact for peers and participate in peer support work. The function of this role is IT based in line with the service objective of being paper light, this will entail fully utilising system one, Microsoft office (including excel and outlook) and other IT equipment such as telephonetics and projectors. The Candidate Pack provides an overview of the key tasks and responsibilities of the role, and the person specification outlines the qualifications, skills, experience and knowledge required. Please view as attached The person specification below is not the full person specification, but outlines the criteria against which your application form will be assessed.

title: Receptionist
description: Join our friendly team at Cranbrook Surgery and make a real difference to our patients and local community. We are looking for a welcoming, organised and motivated Receptionist/Administrator with previous GP surgery experience, who enjoys helping people and working as part of a supportive team. You will be the first point of contact for patients, assisting with appointments, telephone enquiries and essential administrative tasks, while also supporting the Practice Manager with the day-to-day running of the surgery. This is a rewarding opportunity to use your existing skills, develop your experience and contribute to delivering a high-quality service to our patients. You will welcome patients, manage appointment bookings and telephone enquiries, maintain accurate patient records, process incoming correspondence and support the clinical team with daily administrative tasks. You will also assist the Practice Manager with general administration, staff communication, record keeping, updating policies and procedures, monitoring training records and supporting practice operations. You will help ensure patient information is handled confidentially and that the practice runs smoothly, providing a friendly, professional and helpful service to patients and colleagues. Cranbrook Surgery is seeking a friendly, organised and reliable Receptionist/Administrator with previous GP surgery experience to join our busy team in Ilford. Main Duties: Welcome patients and manage appointments and telephone enquiries. Maintain accurate patient records and process correspondence. Provide general administrative support to GPs and clinical staff. Support the Practice Manager with daily operations, staff records, training records and administrative tasks. Maintain confidentiality and follow NHS policies and procedures. Provide a professional, helpful and compassionate service to patients. Essential Requirements: Previous experience working in a GP surgery. Good communication, organisation and IT skills. Knowledge of GP clinical systems, preferably EMIS Web. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. A professional, flexible and confidential approach. We offer a friendly team environment and the opportunity to contribute to high-quality patient care in our local community.

title: Receptionist
description: We are seeking a friendly, organised, reliable and compassionate Receptionist to join our busy NHS GP practice in Southall, serving approximately 5,000 registered patients with a clinical team of 7 GPs. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for patients, providing a professional, welcoming and efficient reception service. The role involves face-to-face, telephone and online patient enquiries, appointment administration and general administrative duties to support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication and customer service skills, a calm and professional manner, and the ability to work effectively in a busy environment while maintaining patient confidentiality and delivering a high standard of care. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner. Check patients in for appointments and update their arrival status on the clinical system. Respond to patient enquiries in person, by telephone and through online communication channels. Assist patients with appointment bookings, cancellations and rearrangements in line with practice procedures. Treat all patients with dignity, respect, sensitivity and confidentiality. Communicate effectively with patients from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds. Manage difficult or distressed patients calmly and professionally, escalating concerns when necessary. Ensure patients who require additional assistance are supported appropriately. 2. Telephone and Appointment Management Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally. Handle appointment requests in accordance with practice policies and access procedures. Direct calls to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Take accurate messages and ensure they are passed to the relevant person in a timely manner. Explain practice procedures, appointment arrangements and available services clearly. Recognise when a call may require urgent clinical attention and follow the practice's approved escalation procedures. Never provide clinical advice beyond the receptionist's level of training and authorised responsibilities. Use the practice's clinical computer system, SystmOne, Use the practice's clinical computer system, such as EMIS Web or SystmOne, as applicable. Register patient arrivals and update demographic and contact details in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain accurate electronic records and administrative information. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence as directed. Scan, code or file documents in accordance with practice protocols and staff training. Support the processing of prescription requests, medical records requests and other administrative tasks within the scope of the role. Assist with recalls, patient registrations, appointment lists and other routine administrative work. Ensure all information is recorded accurately and handled securely. Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, NHS information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures relating to safeguarding children and adults at risk, escalating concerns promptly to the appropriate person. Maintain awareness of confidentiality when speaking on the telephone or at the reception desk. Verify patient identity and follow the practice's procedures before disclosing information. Report any data breaches, confidentiality concerns or incidents to the Practice Manager promptly. Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, managers and other administrative colleagues. Support the daily running of reception, ensuring the reception area remains organised and professional. Assist with incoming post, emails, document handling and general office duties. Follow practice policies, standard operating procedures and health and safety requirements. Attend staff meetings, training sessions and appraisals as required. Assist colleagues during periods of high demand and provide appropriate cover when required. Undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role and level of responsibility.

title: Receptionist
description: Earl's Court Medical Centre has an exciting opportunity for a Medical Receptionist to join our welcoming and forward thinking Practice team on a part-time basis. Your normal pattern of working will be Monday - Friday, within the hours of 8am-6:30pm (5 hours per day). Interested applicants must have primary care and SystmOne experience. Key Responsibilities include: Greeting and assisting patients at the reception desk Managing appointments, cancellations and patients enquiries Answering telephone calls and directing queries appropriately Processing repeat prescription requests Supporting the administrative and clinical team with day-to-day tasks Maintaining confidentially and ensuring accurate record- keeping Processing ingoing and outgoing patient records This is a patient facing role that requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and a calm, efficient approach to working in a fast-paced environment. Reception duties: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 72 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. (including computerised practice notes), ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables (including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc.). Premises: Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Make and serve refreshments for meetings, ensure the kitchen is kept clean and tidy and air and tidy the waiting room in turn with other staff. Covering colleagues holiday and sick cover as required. Process incoming and outgoing mail according to practice protocols. Record actions taken in patient record where appropriate or in accordance with practice protocols. Complete other Daily/ Weekly and Monthly core tasks to support to smooth running of the reception area Any other administration duties as necessitated by the needs of the practice. Confidentiality : In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Act as Chaperone when requested by clinician and in accordance with the Chaperone policy. Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with the Practice policies and procedures, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of their own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for their own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality : The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication : The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Receptionist
description: Blackheath Standard PMS are looking for an experienced and reliable receptionist to join our friendly Reception Team. The practice is situated in a pleasant part of Blackheath in South East London with good transport links and local shops. The position is for 22 hours per week over four days, based on a seven week rolling rota. Please note that the rota is variable and you will be working different days over a seven week period. This is based on a 7am start and 12.30pm finish 8am start and 1pm finish, 1pm start and 6pm finish, 1.30pm start with a 7pm finish. This can vary , depending on the needs of the practice during sickness and annual leave. Flexibility is essential. Saturday mornings are part of our enhanced access service and there is the option to work these sessions on a rotation basis. The duties are variable, depending on what is required on the day. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn. The applicant must have the ability to prioritise workload. Applicants must have the ability to work within a team, have experience of EMIS, AccuRx and Docman and IT skills. Previous experience of working in General Practice is essential, further training will be available for any candidates that show a passion for learning. Job Description Main duties include: Covering reception desk greeting patients and visitors with a professional and friendly manner. Manage the booking system efficiently, signposting patients to the relevant services. Answering incoming calls, respond to queries and manage email correspondence promptly. Assist clinicians as needed, including handling paperwork, stocking consultation rooms and daily end of day duties to ensure the rooms are meeting infection control standards. Manage office supplies, handling incoming/outgoing post and perform general administrative duties. Maintain accurate patient records and ensure confidentiality. The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues. The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment. title: Service Administrator
description: To provide administrative support for the Mental Health Practitioner Service, Health & Wellbeing Coach Service and the Social Prescribing Service. To ensure that all patients referred in are logged and triaged to the appropriate member of each service. To contact patients and provide a service introduction to ensure that expectations are clear. To book initial consultations on behalf of service staff and send reminders to patients. Other agreed administrative tasks as requested and agreed with the service leads, such as meeting notes. To support the Service Leads and H&WB Manager with service reporting, to provide visibility to the GP practices around work done. Responsibilities 1. Referral triage for each service. 2. Booking in and carrying out introduction calls for referrals and sending back inappropriate referrals to referrers. 3. Booking in the initial consultation for each patient with the appropriate service team member. 4. Day to day management and oversight of appointment books, active patient load as well as waiting lists. 5. Sending appointment reminder texts. 6. Oversight of DNAs and focused work on improving the current rates for each service. 7. Manage and oversight of complaints & learning events to ensure a reduction of issues especially around patient bookings. 8. Last minute staff sickness appointment cancellations and communication. 9. Ongoing admin support in the office for team members who travel between many different sites/practices such as letter printing and posting letters to patients. 10. If capacity allows a. Supporting service audit completion b. Uploading compliments to teamnet c. Managing the H&WB Teamnet page d. Supporting at all-staff meetings. e. Helping to organize/attend community events/sessions. 11. Any other reasonable duties required by the Service Leads or Health & Wellbeing Manager in support of the services. This team member would be based in head office at Thomas Wall. Team working Work with the Health & Wellbeing Service Leads and team members. Work with the practice & Sutton PCNs teams to ensure delivery of services and programmes. Actively engage in the performance cycle to identify training and support requirements. Communication The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members as required Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: Receptionist/Administrator Job Overview The Receptionist/Administrator is responsible for providing a professional, welcoming and efficient front-line service to patients while supporting the smooth running of the GP practice. Main responsibilities Welcome patients and deal with enquiries in a friendly and professional manner. Answer telephone calls and respond to patient queries appropriately. Book, cancel and rearrange appointments according to practice procedures. Register new patients and update patient information accurately. Maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive patient information appropriately. Direct patients to the appropriate healthcare professional or service, following practice procedures. Process repeat prescription requests and other administrative tasks where required. Receive and relay messages accurately to GPs and other members of the healthcare team. Deal calmly and professionally with patients who may be upset, anxious or frustrated. Maintain accurate records using the practice's computer systems. Work closely with GPs, nurses, administrators and other members of the practice team. Follow GDPR, confidentiality, safeguarding and health and safety requirements. Support the general administration and smooth day-to-day running of the surgery. Job Summary: The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the Practice including the provision of secretarial/administrative support to clinical staff and other members of the Practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and Responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the Practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. description: Our candidate must be enthusiastic and computer literate, preferably with experience in using EMIS WEB although this is not essential as full training will be given on induction. The role is a wide and varied and the successful candidate will provide a range of administration duties such as summarising, read-coding and searches, managing electronic messages, using own initiative, providing a comprehensive administration/clerical service and attending meetings within the practice. You will be organised, quick thinking, be a problem solver, and be empathetic and caring towards our patients, their families and your colleagues. You will be a person who likes working in a team but you should also be able to take responsibility for getting on with your work supporting the smooth running of the practice. RECEPTION duties. Receiving patients, consulting with members of practice team, processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional. Register new patients, temporary residents and any requiring immediate and necessary treatment, carefully checking all details for accuracy and enter on computer registration link. Taking messages and passing on information. Managing incoming electronic data including clinical documents, patient requests/emails, virtual data and medication request. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and provider. Opening up/locking up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols GENERAL ADMINISTRATION. Processing and distributing incoming and outgoing mail. You who will be the first point of contact for patients, contractors, and visitors as well as carrying out general office management tasks. description: This position is five day a week (Mon to Fri) on site with no remote working. The trust does not offer visa sponsorship for this post. Tyson West 1 is part of Bethlem Royal Hospital. We offer services for men, aged 18-65, who have acute mental illness and require 24 hour hospital care. Acute illnesses start quickly and have distressing symptoms.We provide care for people who live in the London Borough of Croydon.We offer psychiatric assessment, care and treatment in hospital, which helps to reduce the risk to self and others.Our service brings together teams of health and social care professionals, including nurses, psychologists, OTs, social workers and psychiatrists. This position is five day a week on site with no remote working. We are looking for a highly organised, efficient, flexible and proactive person with excellent communication skills to work in the busy post, and who can balance work demands along with the changing needs of the service. The role requires the post holder to communicate with patients, ward staff and visitors, and to develop collaborative working relationships with colleagues and external agencies. The post holder must have an excellent telephone manner, good IT skills with experience using Microsoft Office packages (Work, Excel and Outlook) . Other tasks include, but not limited to, ordering of stationery, processing of post, scanning, monitoring and ordering ward stock and other tasks (see job description). You must be able to prioritise your workload, be effective at implementing good working practices as well as having a flexible and proactive approach to work in order to cover colleagues when required. Be responsible for the provision of a high-quality reception and administrative service for a busy acute ward. Reception:To provide an effective and efficient reception and administrative services, which will include dealing with telephone enquiries, taking accurate messages and pass them promptly to the appropriate member of the team. To monitor supplies of patient information such as welcome packs.Administration:To assist in providing a comprehensive administrative service to the multi-disciplinary teams, which include but not limited to data inputting patient information, scanning documents and uploading to patient database. Maintaining efficient and effective administration systems to support the needs of the service, working with other members of the admin team as appropriate to achieve this. To assist in providing accurate and efficient data entry into Trust information systems and to assist in the collection of statistical information for the Trust. To assist in the booking of interpreters, taxis etc. Service Requirements:To undertake any other duties as required for the service by the Business Manager or Team Leaders.To deliver a high standard of customer care, representative or the service and the overall Trust objectives and commitments. title: Care Navigator/Receptionist
description: Our Receptionists /Care Navigators are key contributors in supporting the smooth running of the practice by providing internal administrative support necessary for the practice team to meet the needs of and caring for our patients. This role provides an accessible, safe and effective line of communication for patients and third parties whether via the phone, email, or in person. The purpose of this supporting role is to ensure that our patients receive an all-around excellent experience every time they visit or contact Clerkenwell Medical Practice. Reception Duties: Book appointments in accordance with the practice protocols and take onboard feedback to assist with effective patient management for the best use of Clerkenwell Medical Practice patient-facing capacity. Receive and make phone calls as required and ensure all queries are dealt with as they arise. Dealing with patient queries and other contacts in order to safely minimise the clinical workload wherever possible Work the reception desk, greeting patients, maintaining the waiting area, and ensuring the desk is well stocked at all times. Management of prescriptions, documents and letters that arrive at the reception desk. Keep the reception desk well stocked and provide consumables for clinical rooms regularly to ensure they are stocked as well as on request. Deal with samples received from patients and provide accurate specimen receptacles for patients asked to provide samples. Supports the practice recall system with accuracy to help us meet our clinical performance targets. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and associated healthcare agencies and providers. Administrative Duties: Work to practice processes, protocols and procedures and according to practice policy all of which will change from time to time. Process and distribute all emails and eConsults and ensure they are directed to the correct member of the practice team. Completing all requests received from the practice team to support clinicians in their admin duties. Completing referrals, chasing hospital appointments, test results, and patient-related information and documentation. Generating letters, sick notes and other documentation for patients at the request of clinicians. Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning. Filing Summarising and coding Docman filing Recalls including cervical cytology, childhood immunisations and any other central database generated services/requirements Checking for outstanding work and making sure no tasks are overlooked or requests/documents are left unprocessed when practice team members are absent Open and distribute the post. Taking responsibility for all outgoing post to be sent in a timely manner bearing the correct postage in order to avoid all unnecessary delays in post leaving the practice Work under pressure with minimal supervision, safely use initiative with the ability to prioritise and also recognise when to ask for information or help Load and unload the dishwasher Buy supplies eg milk for tea and coffee when necessary Maintaining training and skills in order to facilitate the role. Maintain total confidentiality at all times All other responsibilities and tasks not listed here that relate to this post and the smooth running of the practice and/or contribute to role and/or service development at work Requirements: Attention to detail. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Strong IT skills including Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook. Ability to work in a busy and pressured environment, whilst staying organised and prioritising a varied workload. Ability to follow procedures, processes, protocols, and instructions as per CQC requirements. Be enthusiastic and a team player. Be flexible and adaptable. Previous GP or NHS experience desirable but not essential. Previous EMIS and Docman10 experience desirable but not essential If not, familiarity with registering patients, e-referrals, repeat prescriptions, coding, and data entry. Confidentiality In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health and safetyThe post holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice health and safety policy, to include: Using security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Equality and diversityThe post holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional developmentThe post holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work QualityThe post holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Contribution to the implementation of servicesThe post holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how policies, standards and guidelines affect their and others work Participate in audit where appropriate Undertake all duties not listed that relate to this post and the smooth running and development of the practice

title: Medical Receptionist / Admin
description: We are offering a part-time receptionist/administrator, to join our friendly team. To be successful in this role, you will be a friendly, approachable and reliable team player with excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both face-to-face and over the telephone. You will be confident working in a busy environment, able to remain calm under pressure, and capable of managing multiple tasks efficiently while maintaining a high standard of patient service. The successful candidate must be available to start in December 2026. Flexibility is essential, as the role will involve working a variety of shifts, including early starts from 8:00 am and/or late finishes at 8:00 pm. You will also be expected to provide holiday cover when required. Previous experience using EMIS Web is essential. The successful candidate must be confident using the system to support the day-to-day running of the practice and be comfortable using computer systems to manage administrative tasks efficiently. Reception Duties and Responsibilities Welcoming patients and visitors, answering telephone calls, emails and online consultations professionally. Booking appointments via EMIS Web and directing patients to the appropriate clinician or service. Processing medical report requests and cash payments, ensuring requests are completed within agreed timeframes. Printing forms for clinics, including blood tests and X-rays. Providing specimen pots and forms, ensuring dates and times are correctly recorded. Registering new patients and recording clinical information, including blood pressure and weight readings. Maintaining a tidy reception area and replenishing supplies. Supporting distressed or vulnerable patients with empathy and handling challenging situations sensitively. Recalling patients for essential reviews, including diabetes, to support QOF targets. Scanning, coding and filing documents into patient records using Docman. Monitoring and ordering clinical and administrative supplies. Liaising professionally and confidentially with other healthcare departments. Completing mandatory training and contributing to enhanced services, CQC requirements, audits and quality improvement activities. Opening and securing the premises when required. Providing flexible cover for colleagues, including short-notice sickness absence. Additional hours will be reimbursed where agreed in advance, in accordance with practice policy. We are offering a part-time receptionist/administrator, to join our small friendly team. In order to be successful, you must be a good team player with excellent communication skills both face to face and over the telephone, as well as being able to work under pressure and having the ability to multitask. We require someone who is flexible as the position will involve morning shifts (8:00am) and/or late evenings (8:00pm), as well as someone who is willing to cover holidays. You will need to be able to start in December 2026. The practice uses EMIS web as the clinical system, so it is preferable that you have had experience in using this tool or you are computer literate and can adapt to different software systems efficiently. Main duties: - Reception Welcoming patients and visitors, answering calls, emails and online consultations, ensuring needs are met. Booking appointments appropriately via EMIS, directing them to the correct clinician. Assisting patients with medical reports, dealing with cash payments and completing request within the given time frame. Printing and handing out forms for patients to take to different clinics e.g. Blood test and x-ray forms. Supporting patients with specimen pots and forms, making sure the date and time on both forms and sample. Registering new patients and recording clinical information, such as blood pressure readings and weight for monitoring purposes. Keeping reception area tidy, replacing any empty items. Comforting distressed patients, handling with difficult needs. - Admin Recalling patients for vital appointments, such as diabetes reviews, meeting the requirements for QOF. Request and return paper notes as necessary Scanning and Filing in documents via Docman10 into patients records Completing tasks set by clinicians on workflow. Ordering items (clinical and admin) when low, ensuring there is a sufficient stock. Dealing with requests for home visits and recording them on their record. Chasing up appointments and results from hospitals either via phone or email Liaising with other medical departments, such as radiologists or psychologists with professionalism and discretion Ordering ambulances for patients and clinicians, both routinely and in an emergency Completing all mandatory training for quality purposes - General Active involvement in enhanced service, CQC and quality related work. Opening the premises and securing at night, when required. Dealing with problems and queries from the doctors, other staff, attached staff and other organisations. Following and adhering to Practice admin protocols. Be flexible to cover colleagues in their absence including short notice cover for sickness. This may result in longer working hours or different days to normal working days (reimbursement for agreed additional hours worked will be made). - Quality The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. - Equality and Diversity The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with Practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. - Health & Safety The post holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health and safety and security as laid out in the staff handbook and health and safety manual. This will include Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified. This job description is not exhaustive and duties may vary with the requirements of the practice or as directed by the Partners.

title: Digital Receptionist
description: Millway Medical Practice is a large, high-performing NHS GP practice serving ~25,000 patients in Mill Hill, North London. We are looking for a Digital Receptionist / eConsult Coordinator to join our expanding team. This is a key frontline role in a modern, digitally-driven GP practice , focused on managing online patient demand (eConsults) alongside supporting core reception and telephony functions. You will play a crucial role in ensuring patients are navigated safely, efficiently, and compassionately to the right care, at the right time. We can offer full-time or part-time hours for the right candidate. To act as a central point of coordination for online consultations (eConsult) and digital patient access , ensuring: Timely and accurate processing of eConsults Safe navigation of patients to appropriate services Support for reception and phone systems during peak demand High-quality patient experience in a fast-paced environment 1. eConsult & Digital Workflow Management (Primary Function) Monitor and process incoming eConsults throughout the day Triage and allocate requests in line with practice protocols Identify urgent or high-risk submissions and escalate appropriately Book patients into appropriate appointments (GP, ACP, PA pharmacist, etc.) Communicate outcomes to patients via SMS, AccuRx or phone Ensure all eConsults are actioned within agreed timeframes Support optimisation of digital workflows and demand management Answer incoming calls using cloud telephony systems (Surgery Connect) Navigate patients to the most appropriate service (appointments, self-care, pharmacy, etc.) Book, amend and cancel appointments using EMIS Web Support front desk when required, including greeting patients Manage patient queries efficiently and professionally Guide patients through the triage model Promote use of online services (eConsult, NHS App, website) Signpost to appropriate services (community pharmacy, urgent care, etc.) Support vulnerable patients who may struggle with digital access Process registrations and update patient records Handle basic prescription/admin queries Scan and process incoming documents (BetterLetter / Docman where required) Support digital communication campaigns (SMS, website updates) Maintain accurate records and data quality Work collaboratively with reception, admin and clinical teams Provide cover during staff absence or peak demand periods Support onboarding and training of new staff where appropriate

title: Medical Receptionist
description: HAMPSTEAD GROUP PRACTICE (NW3 2QU) Medical Receptionist Full-Time or Part-Time Posts Hourly rate: £ 14.20 Various shifts between 8am to 6.30pm, Monday - Friday We are seeking highly organised, motivated individuals with excellent customer service skills to support our Patient Services Team. Candidates must be computer literate, flexible and able to work under pressure. Previous NHS experience and knowledge of EMIS Web clinical system are preferred but not essential. First point of contact for patients registered with the practice. Answering phone calls and email queries from patients and external organisations. Triaging calls to book patients into the appropriate clinics or signpost patients to appropriate services Dealing with prescription requests and liasing with pharmacies as and when required Providing admin support to clinical team HAMPSTEAD GROUP PRACTICE JOB DESCRIPTION Title: Patient Services Team Accountable to: Practice Manager Reports to: Patient Services Manager Liaises with: Patients and Users of the Practice,Professional Members of the Practice Team,Other Administration Staff JOB SUMMARY The postholder will be responsible for ensuring that an efficient and personable service is provided to all users of the Hampstead Group Practice. title: Care Navigator/Receptionist & Administrator
description: As the first point of contact for patients, you will play a key role in delivering excellent customer service and supporting the smooth running of the practice. Duties include welcoming patients, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, responding to emails, processing prescription requests, filing and coding clinical correspondence and referrals, supporting safeguarding processes, undertaking site checks, monitoring stock levels, and helping maintain a safe environment. Working as part of a team of four, you will contribute to a shared workload and help ensure patients receive the right support at the right time. The role is offered on a split rota of 07:45-13:45 (Week 1) and 13:00-19:00 (Week 2) . Previous experience in a GP practice or similar patient-facing role is essential. Applicants must have 6-12 months' experience and be proficient in EMIS Web . The successful candidate must deliver excellent patient care and customer service while maintaining professionalism and accuracy. If you are a reliable team player with excellent communication skills, attention to detail and a commitment to patient care, we would love to hear from you. As a Patient Care Navigator / Receptionist / Administrator, you will be the first point of contact for patients and visitors, providing a professional, friendly and efficient service. You will welcome patients, respond to enquiries in person and by telephone, and support patients in accessing the most appropriate services. The role includes processing prescription requests, responding to emails, filing and coding clinical correspondence, maintaining accurate patient records, processing referrals via NHS e-Referral Service, actioning eConsults as directed by the clinical team, managing appointments, registering new patients, and handling general enquiries. title: GP Receptionist

We also welcome applicants with strong customer service experience who enjoy helping people, can manage a variety of tasks and are quick to learn new online systems. As a GP Receptionist, you will play an important role in supporting patients and helping the practice run smoothly. Your daily responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors, providing friendly and professional assistance. Responding to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through online systems. Helping patients access appropriate services, including assisting with online appointment requests. Using our clinical system (EMIS Web) and other digital platforms to manage patient information and administrative tasks. Processing patient requests, including prescriptions, test-related enquiries and general correspondence. Supporting GPs, nurses and other team members with day-to-day administrative duties. Job Description GP Receptionist Organisation: Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group Primary Location: Heathway Medical Centre, Dagenham Contract: Full-time, fixed-term until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension Hours: 37.5 hours per week, with varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. Help ensure patients receive clear and accurate information about practice services. 3. Clinical Systems and Digital Administration Use EMIS Web and other practice systems to access and update patient information accurately. title: GP Receptionist
description: Join our friendly team at St Katharine Docks Practice , a welcoming single-handed GP surgery set in the beautiful surroundings of St Katharine Docks, just moments from the Tower of London. We pride ourselves on providing high-quality, personalised care to our patients and creating a supportive, professional, and inclusive workplace. We are looking for a Receptionist to provide cover , helping to ensure the smooth running of our busy front desk. As the first point of contact for patients, youll play a vital role in making every patient feel welcome, listened to, and supported. Youll handle calls, manage appointments, process correspondence, and assist the GP and wider team in delivering excellent service. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys helping others, communicates clearly and kindly, and can stay calm under pressure. Youll need to be organised, confident using computers, and committed to maintaining confidentiality at all times. In return, we offer a friendly working environment, on-the-job training, and opportunities for personal development. Youll be part of a small, close-knit team where your contribution truly makes a difference to the lives of our patients and the success of our practice. If youre reliable, compassionate, and looking for a rewarding role in the heart of London, wed love to hear from you. Welcome and assist patients and visitors in person and over the telephone in a professional and friendly manner. Manage incoming calls, respond to general enquiries, and direct calls as appropriate. Schedule and manage patient appointments using the practice clinical system - EMIS Web. Register new patients and update existing patient information accurately. Handle incoming and outgoing post and emails. Obtain external medical reports, test results, and other documentation as required. Scan and file correspondence and clinical documents. Maintain a tidy, organised, and welcoming reception area. Safeguard patient confidentiality and comply with GDPR and NHS data protection requirements. Provide reassurance and support to patients, maintaining a calm and caring approach. Carry out general administrative duties as required by the GP or Practice Manager. Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 48 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. including computerised practice notes, ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables - including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc..

title: Medical Receptionist

The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the clinical and non clinical teams by undertaking a range of front of house and administrative duties. The role will involve full front of house responsibilities, including welcoming and directing patients, responding to queries and providing a professional and efficient service both in person and over the telephone. title: Personal Assistant
description: As Personal Assistant (PA) to the Patient Experience Director (PED) the post holder will provide comprehensive administrative and business support, ensuring the Director's responsibilities are effectively managed. This includes managing a complex diary, correspondence, communication, coordination and delegation ensuring the Director receives a consistent and high-level of support. title: GP Receptionist
description: We are offering an exciting opportunity to join our hardworking and welcoming GP Practice as a Receptionist, providing vital support and becoming an integral part of our dedicated Team. In this part-time role, no two days are ever the same youll be helping patients, solving problems, and making a real difference in peoples lives. Alongside greeting patients, managing appointments, and handling enquiries with care, youll also take on some important administrative tasks that keep the practice running smoothly. It can be challenging at times, but youll be part of a team that works together, supports one another, and takes pride in delivering excellent patient care. This role comes with full training, so no formal qualifications are required. However, previous experience in a GP practice would be preferential but what matters most is your enthusiasm, reliability, and willingness to learn. What you will be doing day to day As a GP Receptionist, you will be at the heart of our practice, making a real difference to patients and the team. Your role will be varied, rewarding, and sometimes challenging - but always important. Be the first friendly face and voice patients encounter, whether welcoming them in person, answering the phone, or responding to emails. Help patients feel supported by managing appointments, processing referrals, and guiding them through their healthcare journey. Keep communication flowing between patients and healthcare professionals, ensuring everyone has the information they need. Take on key admin tasks that keep the practice running smoothly, from handling queries to maintaining accurate records. Champion safety and standards by following procedures, keeping the environment clean and safe, and supporting governance responsibilities. Work closely with the Deputy Practice Manager to deliver excellent reception and administrative services, contributing to patient care and the wider success of the practice. This is a role where youll be helping people every day, working in a supportive team, and knowing that your contribution truly makes a difference. What youll be doing As a GP Receptionist, youll be the first point of contact for patients and play a key role in keeping the practice running smoothly. Your work will be varied, rewarding, and always important. Welcome patients and visitors in person, on the phone, and by email, making sure they feel supported. Book, change, or cancel appointments and help patients with referrals. Guide patients to the right healthcare professional or service. Arrange home visits when needed and follow simple triage steps. Keep the reception area clean and safe so patients feel comfortable. Spot and report problems to the Deputy Practice Manager. Help improve systems by checking processes and following health and safety rules. Protect patient privacy and treat everyone with dignity and respect. Join team meetings and share ideas to improve patient care. Handle concerns or complaints calmly and kindly. Act as a chaperone when patients need support during appointments. Keep accurate records of patient interactions. Register new patients and update records. Scan and process documents and use clinical IT systems. Use resources wisely and avoid unnecessary waste.

title: Practice Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised, motivated and proactive individual to join The Wapping Group Practice and take the lead in managing our QOF, LES and patient recall systems. This is a temporary maternity cover position, with a fixed-term contract of at least 13 months. Flexible working hours: 25 to 37.5 hours per week . This is an important role within our practice, ensuring patients receive the care they need while helping us achieve our clinical and contractual targets. You will work closely with our clinical, administrative and PCN teams to coordinate recalls, monitor performance, improve processes and ensure accurate clinical coding. We offer a friendly and supportive working environment where you will have the opportunity to take ownership of your work, develop your skills and make a real difference to patient care and practice performance. We will provide the necessary training and support to help you succeed in this role, so you do not need to have experience in every aspect of the job. We are looking for someone who is willing to learn, takes initiative and is committed to delivering high-quality work. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing the practice's QOF, LES and patient recall systems, ensuring patients are contacted, booked and followed up appropriately. The role involves monitoring performance against clinical targets, coordinating recall activities with the administrative and PCN teams, managing appointment availability and ensuring accurate clinical coding on EMIS. You will also oversee childhood immunisation and cervical screening recalls, identify areas for improvement and work closely with the clinical team to maximise practice performance. Key Responsibilities QOF, LES and Target Management Manage and coordinate all QOF, LES and other contractual recall activities to ensure the practice achieves maximum performance against targets. Monitor QOF and LES dashboards regularly, identifying areas where performance needs improvement. Take responsibility for managing all targets comprehensively, ensuring patients are recalled, booked and appropriately coded. Regularly update EMIS searches and review performance dashboards to identify outstanding work and missed opportunities. Work closely with the clinical and administrative teams to ensure all targets are achieved within the required deadlines. Patient Recall Management Manage the practice's recall system from start to finish, ensuring eligible patients are identified, contacted, booked and followed up. Generate, distribute and monitor recall lists, ensuring work is completed accurately and on time. Allocate recall lists to PCN recall staff, monitor their progress and follow up on outstanding tasks. Ensure patients who do not respond to initial recall attempts are followed up appropriately. Send validation letters to patients who have not responded after repeated contact attempts, in line with practice protocols. Ensure accurate records are maintained of all recall attempts, patient responses and outcomes. Clinical Appointment Management Review and adjust clinical appointment sessions on EMIS, adding or removing appointment slots where necessary to support QOF and LES recall activities. Ensure sufficient clinical appointments are available for patients requiring reviews, monitoring, vaccinations and other target-related activities. Liaise with clinicians and the management team to plan appointment capacity according to recall demand and outstanding targets. Clinical Coding and Data Quality Ensure all QOF and LES activities are accurately coded on EMIS to support correct reporting and achievement. Identify missing or incorrect clinical codes and liaise with the relevant clinicians to resolve any issues. Provide training and guidance to administrative and recall staff on correct clinical coding procedures. Keep staff updated on changes to QOF, LES and other relevant coding requirements. Carry out regular data quality checks to ensure completed clinical activities are correctly recorded and reflected in performance reports. Childhood Immunisations and Cervical Screening Manage childhood immunisation recalls and targets, ensuring eligible children are identified, contacted and followed up. Monitor childhood immunisation performance and work with the clinical team to improve uptake and achieve contractual targets. Manage cervical screening recalls comprehensively, ensuring eligible patients are invited, booked and appropriately followed up. Monitor cervical screening uptake and identify patients who are overdue or have not responded to invitations. Ensure cervical screening records are accurately maintained, including coding of colposcopy correspondence and relevant clinical outcomes. Ensure cervical screening referral information is correctly recorded and processed through CSMS where required. Work closely with the clinical team to resolve coding discrepancies and ensure screening activity is accurately reflected in EMIS and performance dashboards. Staff Coordination and Training Coordinate the work of PCN recall staff by allocating tasks, setting priorities and monitoring progress. Provide regular feedback and guidance to ensure recall activities are completed efficiently. Train staff on recall procedures, EMIS searches, clinical coding and changes to contractual requirements. Maintain effective communication between clinical, administrative and PCN teams to ensure a coordinated approach to achieving practice targets. Identify areas for improvement and implement changes to strengthen recall processes and overall performance. Performance Monitoring and Reporting Regularly review QOF, LES, childhood immunisation and cervical screening performance. Identify gaps in achievement and take proactive steps to improve performance before contractual deadlines. Provide regular progress updates to the Practice Manager, highlighting outstanding targets, risks and areas requiring additional support. Ensure the practice maximises appropriate contractual achievement and income through effective recall management, accurate coding and timely completion of clinical activities.

title: Patient Care Administrator

Sort out all patient correspondence in line with protocols. To scan all patient correspondence onto the computer, process correspondence for actioning. To archive old patient correspondence. To send out appointment letters, or contact patients by telephone to change or book appointments. To be responsible for allocated personal tasks towards target achievement. To cover the personal tasks of other reception staff during periods of leave. To collect and provide audit data. To be aware of, and to operate within, practice protocols and guidelines - e.g. confidentiality, health & safety. Services Ensure that the professional image of the practice is maintained through the highest standards of staff behaviour and appearance and the look/appearance of waiting-room facilities.
